plan: [ This is a second-price sealed-bid auction: the winner pays the highest competing bid. In such auctions, bidding your true value is a dominant strategy; it maximizes expected profit and avoids two risks: (1) overbidding can win at a price above value (negative profit), and (2) underbidding can forgo positive-profit wins. With no informative history and only 1 round, there’s no strategic adjustment needed. My value is 6, so I bid exactly 6 to win whenever the second-highest bid is below 6 and pay that lower price, ensuring nonnegative profit when I win. ]

[ This is a second-price auction: if I win, I pay the highest competing bid. With independent private values, the dominant strategy is to bid my true value. Overbidding risks paying above my value if others’ bids exceed 40; underbidding risks losing when I would profit. There’s only one round, so no signaling or learning applies. To maximize expected profit this round, I will bid exactly my value, $40, respecting the $0.1 increment rule. ]

[ This is a second-price sealed-bid auction: if I win, I pay the highest competing bid, not my own. With independent private values and no informative history in a single round, the dominant strategy is truthful bidding. Bidding my exact value ($28) maximizes expected profit and avoids the risk of losing when I would have gained surplus if I shaded. Bids are in $0.1 increments, so 28 is valid. ]
